topIssues.title: kona-node: sequencer stuck in forkchoiceUpdated -38002 loop after derivation force-includes a block off its unsafe chain
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
A kona-node **sequencer** can be permanently wedged — hot-looping `engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV3` at thousands of calls per second until the process is unusable — whenever the engine reorgs its unsafe head while the sequencer has a block build in flight. Derivation force-inclusion after a batcher outage makes that reorg happen deterministically, so a sequencing-window expiry reliably kills the node.

Two independent defects combine:

1. `BuildTask` classifies a `-38002 Invalid forkchoice state` response as a **temporary** error, and the task queue retries temporary errors in an unbounded loop with no backoff. The condition is not transient, so the node never leaves the loop and never resets.
2. `BuildTask` has no staleness guard on the parent it was asked to build on, so it will send the EL a forkchoice state whose `safeBlockHash` is not an ancestor of `headBlockHash` in the first place.

All references below are against `68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327`.

## Observed

On a devnet running a kona-node sequencer + kona-node verifier + batcher (a multi-block PoC branch, #22671 — but nothing in the mechanism is specific to it):

- The batcher submitted batches derivation could not apply.
- The sequencing window expired, so derivation force-included an empty block at height `N+1` whose parent was the last common block `N`, but whose hash differed from the sequencer's own unsafe block at `N+1`.
- The node then emitted `engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV3` → `-38002 Invalid forkchoice state` in a hot loop, thousands per second, until it was dead. It never reorged its unsafe chain onto the derived chain and never recovered.

## Mechanism

**Step 1 — derivation reorgs the unsafe chain (this part works).** The derived attributes for `N+1` fail the consolidation check against the sequencer's block at `N+1`, so [`ConsolidateTask`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/consolidate/task.rs#L271-L281) falls back to `build_and_seal`, and the [`InsertTask`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/insert/task.rs#L98-L110) that finishes it sets `unsafe_head`, `local_safe_head` and `safe_head` to the derived block. The EL and the engine state both end up on the derived chain.

**Step 2 — the sequencer submits a build against the pre-reorg head.** `SequencerActor::build_unsealed_payload` reads the unsafe head from a watch channel *once*, at [actor.rs#L217](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/actors/sequencer/actor.rs#L217), then does two pieces of network-bound async work (L1 origin selection, then `prepare_payload_attributes`, which fetches L1 receipts) before [submitting the build at L246](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/actors/sequencer/actor.rs#L245-L246). The `EngineActor` republishes the unsafe head only at the top of its step loop, [after draining the queue](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/actors/engine/actor.rs#L224-L231). So the snapshot the sequencer built against is routinely stale by the time the request lands — a window of hundreds of milliseconds, and the step-1 reorg falls squarely inside it.

**Step 3 — the FCU is rejected.** [`BuildTask::start_build`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/build/task.rs#L104-L110) overrides only the head with the attributes' parent and keeps the state's `safe_head`:

```rust
let new_forkchoice = state
    .sync_state
    .apply_update(EngineSyncStateUpdate { unsafe_head: Some(attributes_envelope.parent), ..Default::default() })
    .create_forkchoice_state();
```

`head = <pre-reorg sequencer block>`, `safe = <derived block>`. The derived block is not an ancestor of the pre-reorg head, so the EL answers `-38002`.

**Step 4 — the hot loop.** `-38002` arrives as a JSON-RPC error and is mapped unconditionally to [`EngineBuildError::AttributesInsertionFailed`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/build/task.rs#L132), which carries severity [`Temporary`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/build/error.rs#L62-L68). `EngineTask::execute` retries temporary errors [in a `while let Err(..)` loop whose only pause is `yield_now().await`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/task.rs#L216-L231) — no backoff, no attempt cap. The forkchoice state is a function of engine state that nothing else can change while the queue is draining, so the retry can never succeed. That is the thousands-of-FCUs-per-second symptom.

**Step 5 — total wedge.** The loop lives inside `Engine::drain`, which the `EngineActor` runs *before* receiving its next request, so the actor can no longer process anything — including a `Reset` request. Meanwhile the sequencer is parked in `start_build_block` awaiting a payload id that will never arrive, so it cannot ask for that reset either. Nothing in the process can break the cycle.

Note the asymmetry that makes this a plain bug rather than a design trade-off: the attribute-less forkchoice update in `SynchronizeTask` **does** special-case the same error code, mapping it to [`SynchronizeTaskError::InvalidForkchoiceState`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/synchronize/task.rs#L125-L135) with severity `Reset`. Only the build path is missing it.

## op-node comparison

op-node guards the same two points, and this is where the fix comes from.

- **Stale parent.** [`EngineController.startBuild`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/op-node/rollup/engine/build_start.go#L57-L65) refuses a sequencer build whose parent is not the current unsafe head, before any engine call:

  ```go
  if !attrs.IsDerived() && attrs.Parent.ID() != e.unsafeHead.ID() {
      e.log.Warn("dropping stale sequencer build start", ...)
      e.requestForkchoiceUpdate(ctx)   // sequencer restarts on the current unsafe head
      return nil, ErrStaleBuild
  }
  ```

  The `!attrs.IsDerived()` condition matters: a derivation-driven reorg legitimately builds on a parent that differs from the unsafe head.

- **`-38002` from the pre-block-creation FCU.** [`startPayload`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go#L1476-L1483) classifies it as `BlockInsertPrestateErr` — "pre-block-creation forkchoice update was inconsistent with engine, need reset to resolve" — which `startBuild` turns into a [`ResetEvent`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/op-node/rollup/engine/build_start.go#L104-L109), never a retry.

op-node has also already been bitten by the adjacent oscillation: see the `#21119` comment in [`FollowSource`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go#L1578-L1590) — "head on the fork, safe on upstream -> InvalidForkchoiceState -> reset re-selects the fork -> oscillation" — fixed there with a `forceReset` that lands head and safe in one shot.

## Proposed fix

1. Map `-38002` in `BuildTask::start_build` to a new `EngineBuildError::InvalidForkchoiceState` with severity `Reset`, mirroring `SynchronizeTask` and op-node's `startPayload`.
2. Give `BuildTask` op-node's stale-parent guard, gated on the existing `BuildSealCoupling` flag that `SealTask` already uses for exactly this distinction (`Atomic` = derivation-driven, parent chosen from engine state, skip the check; `Detached` = external caller working from its own snapshot, check it). Report the rejection to the caller over the result channel instead of leaving it waiting.
3. Have the sequencer treat a rejected or dropped build as "re-build on the new head next tick" rather than a fatal actor error — every `NodeActor::step` error [shuts the whole node down](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/68b009443f67cf830990e913bcbde8536cb15327/rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/service/util.rs#L28-L38).
4. Publish the unsafe head after an engine reset as well, so the sequencer cannot build against a pre-reset snapshot.

Worth considering separately, not covered by the above: the task queue's temporary-error retry has no backoff at all. Any genuinely temporary engine error currently spins the engine as fast as the EL will answer. op-node's equivalent yields to a driver that re-attempts on a timer.

## Repro status

Not reproduced as an automated test. The Rust-side mechanism is covered by unit tests in the fix PR (a `-38002` build must surface as `Reset` and must not be retried; a stale detached build must be rejected without touching the engine; the sequencer must retry rather than die). A full-system repro is blocked on a harness gap:

- **No test anywhere exercises batcher outage → sequencing-window expiry → force-include → sequencer unsafe-chain reorg against a kona-node sequencer.** Not in `op-acceptance-tests/`, not in `rust/kona/tests/node/`, not in Rust.
- The one test that models the whole loop end-to-end, `TestSequencingWindowExpiry` (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/seqwindow/expiry_test.go`), is bound to `presets.NewTwoL2SupernodeInterop`. Supernode presets never route through `startL2CLForKey`, so they have no `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND` branch and cannot start a `KonaNode`.
- Every op-e2e action test that asserts force-inclusion or post-expiry recovery (`TestL2Verifier_SequenceWindow`, `TestL2Sequencer_SequencerOnlyReorg`, `ExtendedTimeWithoutL1Batches`, `DeepReorg`) drives the in-process Go `L2Sequencer` object directly. There is no engine-API boundary to swap, so they can never target an external CL process. `rust/kona/tests/proofs/sequence_window_expiry_test.go` describes exactly this scenario but its sequencer is op-node — kona only appears there as `kona-host`.
- `rust/kona/tests/node/` has no derivation-stress package (`node/common`, `node/reorgs`, `node/restart`), and `NewMixedOpKona`/`NewMixedOpKonaForConfig` do not accept deployer options, so that preset cannot set a small `sequencerWindowSize` without a signature change.

The gap is fillable: `presets.NewMinimal(t, presets.WithDeployerOptions(sysgo.WithSequencingWindow(N)))` is accepted by the minimal preset, `startL2CLForKey` honours `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND=kona-node`, and the whole acceptance suite already runs against kona-node in the required `memory-all-kona-op-reth-fusaka` CI job. `dsl.L2Batcher.Stop()/Start()` and `dsl.L2CLNode.SetSequencerRecoverMode` all exist and kona implements `admin_setRecoverMode`. What is missing is the test itself. One risk worth flagging for whoever writes it: kona's derivation is gated behind EL-sync completion, which only completes after a P2P-delivered unsafe payload (see the note at `op-acceptance-tests/tests/sdm/init_test.go`).

topIssues.title: kona-gossip: Don't block the network actor on DNS lookups when dialing
topIssues.author: aakoshh
topIssues.body:
The connection gater resolves `/dns`, `/dns4` and `/dns6` addresses with a blocking lookup on the network actor's task, before every dial. A slow or unreachable resolver stalls gossip, block forwarding and the p2p RPC for as long as the lookup takes. Found while working on #23430.

### Current behaviour
- `ConnectionGater::can_dial` ([gater.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/360c2f2e7fd2e4f8c85ef1e1677e6cab4c4de82f/rust/kona/crates/node/gossip/src/gater.rs#L270)) calls `ip_to_check` ([gater.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/360c2f2e7fd2e4f8c85ef1e1677e6cab4c4de82f/rust/kona/crates/node/gossip/src/gater.rs#L225)), which calls `try_resolve_dns` ([gater.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/360c2f2e7fd2e4f8c85ef1e1677e6cab4c4de82f/rust/kona/crates/node/gossip/src/gater.rs#L165)). That uses `to_socket_addrs()` ([gater.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/360c2f2e7fd2e4f8c85ef1e1677e6cab4c4de82f/rust/kona/crates/node/gossip/src/gater.rs#L179)), a blocking `getaddrinfo` call.
- `can_dial` runs inside `GossipDriver::dial_peer`, on the task that also drives the swarm.
- The lookup only serves the blocked IP and subnet checks. When it dials, libp2p-dns resolves the name again, asynchronously, and that's the address it connects to.

### Why it matters more now
With static peers (#23430):
- a node dials each disconnected static peer, at each of its addresses, every minute, and about a second after a static peer disconnects;
- the docs recommend `/dns4/...` addresses for static peers, so their IPs can change.

So a static peer whose name doesn't resolve quickly blocks the network actor regularly, and several such addresses block it one after another.

### Options
- Resolve in `spawn_blocking`, or with an async resolver such as hickory, and finish the dial once the IP is known.
- Skip the IP check before dialing a DNS address, and check the IP the connection actually has once it's established. Checking inbound connections in #23715 needs the same kind of check on established connections.

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock,op-core,op-interop-filter,kona!: per-message interop expiry and SuperchainETHBridge refunds
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Interop executing messages can't be forced in through deposits, so a destination sequencer that refuses to relay a message can keep it from ever being delivered. For `SuperchainETHBridge.sendETH`, that strands the ETH: it is burned on the source chain and never minted on the destination.

This PR lets the source chain learn, through censorship-resistant paths only, that a message can never be delivered. It exposes that per message as `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger.expiredMessages(messageHash)`. `SuperchainETHBridge.refundETH` uses it to give the ETH back.

It replaces #22601, rebuilt on current `develop`. There is no registry, no admin setter, no app callback and no configurable window.

BREAKING CHANGE: `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger.resendMessage` is removed, and the messenger now rejects messages whose target is the `L2CrossDomainMessenger` or the `L2ToL1MessagePasser` (`MessageTargetUnsafe`).
- **Who is affected:** applications and relayers that resend unrelayed interop messages, and anyone sending cross-chain messages to those two targets.
- **What breaks:** a message that isn't relayed within the expiry window can no longer be revived.
- **Configuration:** op-core and kona now refuse to load a dependency set whose `overrideMessageExpiryWindow` exceeds 604800 seconds (7 days), and `op-interop-filter` refuses `--message-expiry-window` above 168h. Operators with a longer override must lower it.
- **Migration:** treat an unrelayed message as expired, and undo the send on the source chain after `expiredMessages(messageHash)` is set, as `SuperchainETHBridge.refundETH` does. To reach L1 or the L2 messenger from a relayed message, go through your own contract.

## The protocol fact it builds on

An executing message is invalid when its block is more than the message expiry window (7 days) after its initiating message's block. Both cross-safety (op-supernode) and the fault proof (kona) enforce this, comparing the same two timestamps.

So once a destination's clock passes `sendTime + window` and the message is still unrelayed, no valid block can relay it. This PR carries that fact back to the source chain over a withdrawal followed by a deposit.

## How it works

For a message `H` sent from A to B and never relayed on B:

1. **On A, at send time:** `sendMessage` stores `sentMessageTimestamps[H] = block.timestamp`.
2. **On B, export:** anyone calls `UndeliveredMessageExporter.exportUndeliveredMessage(sourceMessenger, source, nonce, sender, target, message, minGasLimit)`. This is a new predeploy at `0x…0030`.
   - It hashes the message with **B's own chain ID as the destination**, so a chain can only speak for messages addressed to it.
   - It requires `!L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger.successfulMessages(H)`.
   - It sends `relayUndeliveredMessage(H, block.timestamp)` to `sourceMessenger`, which is A's `L1CrossDomainMessenger`, through the `L2CrossDomainMessenger`.
   - This is not an executing message, so if B censors it, it can be forced in as a deposit. The acceptance test does exactly that.
3. **On L1:** B's `L1CrossDomainMessenger` relays the withdrawal into A's `L1CrossDomainMessenger.relayUndeliveredMessage`. The function first requires that A has the `INTEROP` feature enabled. It then accepts the call only if:
   - the caller is a real `L1CrossDomainMessenger`: its portal's `SystemConfig` names it as that chain's messenger;
   - the caller's portal is authorized by **A's `ETHLockbox`**, meaning it is in A's cluster;
   - the L2 sender of the withdrawal is the **`UndeliveredMessageExporter`**.

   It then sends `expireMessage(H, undeliveredAt)` to A's `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger` as a deposit.
4. **On A, expire:** `expireMessage` accepts only the `L2CrossDomainMessenger` relaying from A's own `L1CrossDomainMessenger`, which is `otherMessenger()`, so L2 needs no new address. If `undeliveredAt > sentMessageTimestamps[H] + EXPIRY_PERIOD`, it sets `expiredMessages[H] = true`.
5. **On A, refund:** anyone calls `SuperchainETHBridge.refundETH(destination, nonce, from, to, amount)`. It rebuilds `H` from those arguments, requires `expiredMessages[H]`, and refunds `from` exactly once with a forced send.

**Why a refund can't double-spend:** B attests that H was unrelayed at a time past the window, and from then on the protocol rejects any relay of H. A acts only on a fact dated past `EXPIRY_PERIOD`, measured from a send time that is written once and never changes.

### Why the trusted sender is a new predeploy

The L1 side trusts withdrawals from the `UndeliveredMessageExporter` at `0x…0030`. It does not trust the `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger`.
- **No forged withdrawal can predate the upgrade.** The proxy at `0x…0030` had no implementation until this upgrade, so no withdrawal from it exists from before.
- **It can't be impersonated.** The exporter makes exactly one kind of call, so nothing can make it say something it didn't check.

The messenger, by contrast, has a history of relaying messages to arbitrary targets. Trusting it would let forged withdrawals created before the upgrade wait in unfinalized withdrawals or failed messages and be replayed afterwards. It would also open a window during any L1-before-L2 rollout.

### What prevents each attack
- **Forged facts from other chains:** every chain whose portal A's lockbox authorizes can already withdraw A's ETH, so trusting its facts adds no trust.
- **A forged messenger borrowing a real portal:** it fails the reverse binding.
- **Governance of another cluster chain:** that chain's governance could upgrade its own exporter and forge facts about any destination. That is the same trust as the shared `ETHLockbox` already places in it, since lockbox portals must share one proxy admin owner.
- **Something else sending the deposit as A's L1 messenger:** `L1CrossDomainMessenger` already refuses to relay messages that target itself, so only `relayUndeliveredMessage` can make it the sender.
- **The L1 call runs out of gas:** it lands in the calling messenger's failed messages, and anyone can replay it.
- **The wrong source messenger is named:** the deposit reverts on a chain that never sent `H`, and anyone can export again.
- **A fact that arrives too early:** it fails on A with `MessageNotExpired`. It can never succeed later, because its timestamp is fixed.

## Behavior changes (please review these closely)

- **`resendMessage` is removed** (`L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger` 2.0.0).
  - **Why:** resending lets a message be relayed for another window, which conflicts with expiry: a sender could resend, take a refund, and then have the resent event relayed. And letting anyone resend would let anyone stop a message from ever expiring.
  - **What happens instead:** an unrelayed message expires, and the app undoes the send.
  - **Who loses out:** apps without a refund, such as `SuperchainTokenBridge` today, lose the ability to revive an unrelayed message until they add one. See follow-ups.
- **The messenger refuses unsafe targets.** It won't send or relay messages whose target is the `L2CrossDomainMessenger` or the `L2ToL1MessagePasser` (`MessageTargetUnsafe`).
  - **This is defense in depth:** expiry's safety doesn't depend on it.
  - **What it guarantees:** the messenger never starts a withdrawal. Nothing that trusts it as a withdrawal sender, today or in future L1 contracts, can be fooled by a relayed message.
- **The expiry window can't exceed 7 days.** op-core and kona both reject a dependency-set message expiry window override above 7 days, and `op-interop-filter` caps its `--message-expiry-window` flag the same way. A window longer than the contract's period would allow a refund followed by a valid relay.
- **`EXPIRY_PERIOD = 8 days`:** the protocol's 7-day window plus a 1-day safety margin.
- **Every message costs more gas:** `sendMessage` stores a timestamp, about 22k more gas per message.
- **Old messages can't expire:** messages sent before this upgrade have no timestamp.

## Contract changes

- **`L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger` 1.3.2 → 2.0.0:**
  - new constant `EXPIRY_PERIOD`;
  - new storage at slots 3–4: `sentMessageTimestamps` and `expiredMessages`;
  - new function `expireMessage`, the unsafe-target helper, and `resendMessage` removed;
  - no initializer, so it is still upgraded with plain `upgradeTo`.
- **New `UndeliveredMessageExporter` 1.0.0 at `0x…0030`:** gated on interop like the other interop predeploys, and wired through `Predeploys`, `L2Genesis`, `L2ContractsManager` (now 1.15.0), the Go predeploy registry and the NUT bundle.
- **`L1CrossDomainMessenger` 2.11.1 → 2.12.0:** adds `relayUndeliveredMessage`, with no new storage and an `INTEROP` gate. `EXPIRE_MESSAGE_GAS_LIMIT = 100_000`, which a cold-storage relay test exercises.
- **`SuperchainETHBridge` 1.0.1 → 1.1.0:** `sendETH` is unchanged. Adds `refundETH` and a `refunded` mapping.
- **Off-chain:** the window cap in op-core (Go), kona (Rust) and `op-interop-filter`.
- **Docs:** `message-expiration.mdx` and the interop overview now describe expiry instead of resend.

## Launch checklist

- **The window cap is live before expiry is relied on.** Every node and the accepted proof program must enforce the dependency-set window cap of 7 days or less. With an older prestate that accepts a longer override, a refund could be followed by a valid relay.
- **The dependency set and the lockbox agree.** Every chain in a cluster's dependency set must also be authorized in the cluster's `ETHLockbox` and run the exporter, in the same fork. Otherwise sends to it can't be refunded.
- **Embed each cluster's dependency set in the prestate.** It must be in the registry and the absolute prestate: kona falls back to a host-supplied dependency set for clusters that aren't in the registry.
- **Re-snapshot Lagoon after merge.** Lagoon's NUT bundle (`op-core/nuts/fork_lock.toml`) still locks the old messenger. It must be re-snapshotted once this merges, together with kona's bundle counts, and the exporter added back to op-core's `Predeploys` map at that snapshot. It is deliberately left out until then, so the frozen fork state stays unchanged.
- **Rules every future upgrade must keep:**
  - nothing may re-emit `SentMessage` for a message that already has a timestamp: no resend, and no rollback to an implementation that has `resendMessage`;
  - every way of relaying on the destination must set `successfulMessages`;
  - any change to message hashing or nonce versioning must be mirrored in the exporter.

  Breaking any of these allows a refund followed by a relay.
- **Use enough L1 gas when finalizing an export,** at least 1M. Because a failed relay is stored rather than reverted, `eth_estimateGas` under-estimates.

## Limitations

- **Messages sent before the upgrade can't be recovered.** They have no send timestamp, so they can never expire, and with `resendMessage` gone they can't be resent either. In production this ships with interop's launch, so no messages predate it.
- **`refundETH` always pays `from`,** which is `sendETH`'s `msg.sender`. A router that sent ETH on someone's behalf needs its own way to pass a refund on. If `sendETH` was itself called from a relayed interop message, `from` is the `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger`, and a refund would be stuck there.
- **An early export is harmless.** It fails on the source with `MessageNotExpired`. Export again after `EXPIRY_PERIOD`.

## Testing

- **Forge:**
  - messenger: send timestamps, the unsafe-target rule on send and on relay, `expireMessage` auth and the exact boundary, and `expireMessage` through a real `L2CrossDomainMessenger` relay with cold storage, including an out-of-gas run then a replay;
  - exporter: hashing, the delivered check, and an export forced in from a deposit;
  - `L1CrossDomainMessenger`: an integration test with real contracts; rejection of a forged messenger, another lockbox, the wrong L2 sender (including `0x…23`), interop disabled, and the chain's own messenger;
  - bridge: refund after expiry pays exactly once; a forged refund through a direct `sendMessage` reverts; wrong-preimage fuzzing;
  - one end-to-end test of send → export → L1 → expire → refund, using `vm.warp`.
- **Acceptance (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/expiry`, two-chain interop devnet):** every leg runs for real:
  - `sendETH` from A, never relayed on B;
  - an export **forced in as an L1 deposit** on B;
  - prove and finalize, then A's L1 messenger relays and the deposit lands on A.

  The devnet can't advance L2 time 8 days, so the test then asserts the exact `MessageNotExpired` rejection, the carried hash and the timestamp. Forge covers the expired path. The acceptance test also checks ordinary relays and that exporting a delivered message is refused.
- **Go and Rust:** tests for the window cap, and tests pinning the constants.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- A spec section.
- Refunds in `SuperchainTokenBridge`, using the same `expiredMessages` check.
- Formal models and proofs, in a stacked draft PR: Lean, Quint, Kontrol, Halmos and invariant fuzzing.

topPRs.title: kona-node,kona-gossip,kona-peers,kona-disc!: Support static peers
topPRs.author: aakoshh
topPRs.body:
**What**
kona-node can be given static peers with `--p2p.static-peers` (or op-node's name, `--p2p.static`). It dials them at startup, dials the ones that aren't connected again every minute and about a second after one disconnects, keeps them protected, and never bans them for their score. Discovery never learns about them, so a node can sit behind a hub without becoming discoverable. This is part 2 of #23430, after #23661.

Closes #23430.

**Why**
Without discovery, which sequencers usually turn off, kona-node had no way to keep connections to known nodes: bootnodes only seed discovery. Building and testing this surfaced several bugs, fixed here in their own commits:
- `--p2p.ban.peers` did nothing: the gossip builder never passed peer monitoring to the driver. Peers below `--p2p.ban.threshold` are now banned.
- Peer scores barely decayed: `score_decay` aimed for `1 - DecayToZero` (0.99) where op-node uses `DecayToZero` (0.01), so penalties lasted about 100 times longer than in op-node. Scores now decay as in op-node, which changes scoring for every node running the default `--p2p.scoring light`.
- Scoring parameters that gossipsub rejects, such as a block time under a second, logged a warning and left the node running without scoring. The node now refuses to start, like op-node.
- A malformed `--p2p.bootnodes` entry panicked while building the config. It is now a CLI error, and an empty `KONA_NODE_P2P_BOOTNODES` or `KONA_NODE_P2P_STATIC_PEERS` means an empty list.
- Discovery hands over the ENRs of connected peers all the time, and each one went through the dialing path. The network actor now skips them, so `kona_node_dial_peer_error{type="already_connected"}`, the "Already connected" series of the "Peers Dialed / min" dashboard panel, drops to nearly zero.

**How**
- A static peer listed with several addresses is one peer, dialed once with all of them. libp2p tries them in parallel and keeps the first that connects, as go-libp2p does for op-node. The gate checks each address, and `ConnectionGate::dialing` now takes the peer ID.
- Redials run on a deadline that `GossipDriver::next` turns into `Event::StaticPeersDue`, the same pattern as closing duplicate connections from #23661.
- op-node keeps protection per tag, so `opp2p_unprotectPeer` only removes the API's tag. kona's gater has no tags, so `GossipDriver::unprotect_peer` leaves static peers protected instead.
- Static peers are exempt from score bans, like op-node's `IsStatic`, but not from operator blocks: a blocked static peer isn't dialed until it is unblocked.
- Dropping a `GossipDriver` removes its listener. libp2p's memory transport keeps a process-wide registry of ports and only frees one in `remove_listener`, not when the transport or listener is dropped, so a restarted in-memory test node couldn't listen on its address again. That's a libp2p bug to report upstream.

**Caveats**
- The environment variable is `KONA_NODE_P2P_STATIC_PEERS`, as the issue asks, not the prefix-swapped `KONA_NODE_P2P_STATIC`: clap allows one variable per flag.
- `--p2p.no-discovery` still isn't applied (#23702), so static peers run alongside discovery. The tests show static peering without discovery by giving nodes no bootnodes.
- The gate resolves a `/dns*` static peer's name with a blocking lookup on the network actor's task, on every dial of a disconnected static peer (#23725).
- A static peer that accepts the connection and then closes it straight away is dialed again about every second, with no backoff. The redial backoff in #23698 should cover static peers too.
- Log messages that changed, for anyone alerting on them: "Peer scoring failed" is now a startup error; "Failed to disconnect peer" is now "Cannot disconnect a peer that isn't connected"; the ban handler's "non-existing peer" warning is gone.

**Alternatives**
- Tags in the gater, as op-node has, instead of checking the driver's static peers when unprotecting. Static peers are the only second reason for protection, so the check is enough.
- Parsing the whole comma-separated list in one parser. It would skip empty entries, but a repeated flag would then be an error; per-entry parsing keeps the usual clap behaviour.
- Review findings dismissed (`rust-code-reviewer`, `deletion-reviewer`):
  - Skip static peers whose dial is still in flight at the next check: the `already_dialing` error each minute is a useful sign of a stuck dial.
  - Reject a zero redial interval or reconnect delay: only tests can set them, and no other interval in kona-node is checked.
  - `ConnectionGate::is_blocked_addr` has no caller outside the gater yet; it's there for symmetry with `is_blocked_peer`, and #23715 will need it.
  - Make `group_by_peer` an associated function: it returns a map, not a `PeerAddr`.
  - Pings record the connection duration so far as well. That's older behaviour, kept; the test checks when the duration is recorded, not how many samples there are.
  - The gater's own `invalid_multiaddr` check is no longer reachable from code in the repo, but `can_dial` is public, so it stays.

**Potential follow-ups**
Opened as issues: the redial limit (#23698), gauges that should be counters (#23699), connection limits and per-peer state that only grows (#23700), the write-only `connectedness` map (#23701), `--p2p.no-discovery` (#23702), blocks that don't apply to inbound connections (#23715), and the blocking DNS lookup (#23725). Not tracked yet:
- `opp2p_connectPeer` doesn't wait for the connection: its retry only retries on errors, and the call returns `Ok(false)`.
- `GossipDriver` exposes runtime state as public fields that the network actor reaches into.
- The libp2p memory transport bug above, upstream.

BREAKING CHANGE: For operators: the node no longer starts with peer scoring parameters gossipsub rejects, or with a malformed `--p2p.bootnodes` entry; `--p2p.ban.peers` now bans; scores decay faster, as in op-node. For users of the crates: `GossipDriver::dial(Enr)` is replaced by `enr_to_peer_addr` and `dial_peer`; `ConnectionGate::dialing` takes a `&PeerId`, and implementations need the new `is_blocked_peer` and `is_blocked_addr` methods; `NetworkConfig` has a new `static_peers` field; `GossipDriver::peer_connection_start` holds `tokio::time::Instant`s; `DialInfo` and `ConnectionGater::dialed_peers` (now `dialed_addrs`) are no longer public; `BootNode::parse_bootnode` returns a `Result`; `HandlerRequest::BanAddrs` takes a plain `HashSet`.

topPRs.title: kona-node,kona-engine!: recover stale sequencer builds after reorgs
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
A derivation reorg can leave the sequencer building on an old unsafe head; an inconsistent forkchoice then traps it retrying work that cannot succeed. Sequencing now discards stale builds, recovers from invalid forkchoice, and retries with fresh attributes without stopping the node.

Sixth PR in the stack, based on #23223: #23268 → #23258 → #23229 → #23581 → #23223 → this PR. The task/helper split keeps the sequencer-only parent check out of derivation without reintroducing `BuildSealCoupling`. Supersedes the focused fix in #23544; leave that PR open pending review. Closes #22681.

Validation: all 344 affected engine/RPC/service/node tests pass, as does the full workspace Rust lint workflow (formatting, strict Clippy, documentation, and upstream-mirror checks). The stale-parent, invalid-forkchoice, and sequencer-retry regressions fail when their fixes are disabled. Rust and deletion/API reviews completed with all findings addressed. All required CI gates pass, including Rust end-to-end tests and both memory acceptance suites. Full-system batcher-outage/forced-inclusion validation is not claimed.

BREAKING CHANGE: Rust integrators must give `BuildTask::new` a mandatory `Sender<Result<PayloadId, BuildTaskError>>` and consume the build outcome from that channel; task execution now returns `()`. `BuildRequest::result_tx` carries the same result. Remove matches on `BuildTaskError::MpscSend` and handle `StaleBuild`; construct `EngineBuildError::AttributesInsertionFailed` with an `Arc` instead of using the removed `From<RpcError>` conversion.

topPRs.title: op-revm,kona-client: lower BLS12-381 precompile input limits at Lagoon
topPRs.author: pauldowman
topPRs.body:
At Lagoon, the BLS12-381 G1MSM, G2MSM and pairing precompiles reject inputs larger than 817 points, 454 points and 340 pairs. Karst keeps the Jovian limits.

This is a consensus change for chains that activate Lagoon: op-reth and kona-client must upgrade together, and the kona-client absolute prestate changes. No chain in the superchain-registry has a Lagoon activation time yet. Interop devnets already running Lagoon need op-reth and the prestate redeployed together.

topPRs.title: op-node,kona: test that derivation ignores SystemConfig PrivateConfigUpdate logs
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
OP Private settlement chains emit `PrivateConfigUpdate(uint256,uint256,uint8,bytes)` from their L1 `SystemConfig` to configure their private chains (#23717). Stock derivation must not treat these logs as config updates for the settlement chain itself.

This adds regression tests in op-node (`TestUpdateSystemConfigIgnoresPrivateConfigUpdate`) and kona (`test_update_with_receipts_ignores_private_config_update`). In each, a receipt mixes a normal `ConfigUpdate` GAS_LIMIT log with `PrivateConfigUpdate` GAS_LIMIT and UNSAFE_BLOCK_SIGNER logs, and only the normal update is applied, with no errors. The private GAS_LIMIT log comes after the normal one, so the test fails if it is ever applied.

Only test code changes. The event topic is computed locally in each test and pinned as `0x4fcb51ee…3948860`.
